solutionText:

both scenarios, sharing of electrons occurs
between phosphorus and chlorine atoms,
resulting in covalent bonds.

solutionText:
In considering the reactivity of compounds
towards nucleophilic addition reactions, two
primary factors need to be evaluated: the
positive character of the electrophilic center
and the degree of steric hindrance.
Electrophilic Character: The more positive
the electrophilic center, the more reactive it is
towards 
a 
nucleophile. 
This 
is 
typically
observed in aldehydes, where the electron-
withdrawing effect of the carbonyl group is not
counterbalanced by additional alkyl groups.
Steric 
Hindrance: 
As 
steric 
hindrance
increases, 
reactivity 
decreases. 
Larger
substituents around the electrophilic center
can block the approach of the nucleophile,
thus lowering the reaction rate.
Given these considerations, aldehydes are
generally more reactive than ketones due to
less steric hindrance and a higher degree of
positive charge on the carbonyl carbon.
Between ketones, those with smaller alkyl
groups are usually more reactive. Evaluate
each compound based on these criteria to
determine

in

Which of the following has most acidic

solutionText:
Trichloroacetic acid (Option C) is the strongest
acid. Here’s why:
Electron-withdrawing effect
Chlorine atoms pull electron density away
from 
the 
–COOH 
group, 
stabilizing 
the
conjugate base (the carboxylate anion).
More Cl → greater stabilization → stronger acid.
Comparative pKa values
Propanoic acid, CH3CH2COOH: pKa ≈ 4.87
Chloroacetic acid, ClCH2COOH: pKa ≈ 2.86
Dichloroacetic acid, Cl2CHCOOH: pKa ≈ 1.25

Since trichloroacetic acid has the lowest pKa, it
donates its proton most readily and is thus the
most acidic.

solutionText:
The incorrect statements are (b), (d) and (e), so
the correct choice is Option B.

depend on how strong the intermolecular
forces are—you must supply enough energy to
